slices.rationale: The timeline surface exists and owns rendering, but there is no trustworthy 50-track edit, seek, playback, and save performance budget.
No tracked compound model, command, or render owner was found; ordinary Clip and build_render_plan are not evidence of nested compound semantics.
No tracked multicam source, synchronization, or non-destructive angle-switch identifier was found.
Two documentation headings describe one shared state-boundary slice. Existing store tests do not prove the complete Rust-projection and pure-selector boundary.
TimelineContainer imports and calls the snap and geometry owners, but the full sticky, multi-target, and both 1.5x threshold acceptance matrix is absent.
Twelve headings and umbrella records converge on one visual surface. Existing canvas tests are partial and do not prove complete visual order, state, and geometry parity.
The shared interaction owners and partial tests exist, but the complete documented selection, drag, trim, scrub, drop, and context-menu matrix is not covered.
Preview imports and mounts the playback and overlay owners, but existing tests emphasize routing and transform behavior rather than the complete control surface.
A non-passive wheel owner distinguishes pinch, modifier zoom, and pan, but there is no focused automated gesture acceptance.
Tracked owners implement a single constant speed only; no editable nonlinear curve model or preview/export parity exists.
The enum and sampler support only linear, hold, and smooth; advanced easing remains unimplemented.
No tracked RGB curve model or editor was found; generic color-grade and color conversion code are not curve ownership.
The desktop-to-Rust call chain exists with strong backend tests; a focused desktop component acceptance is the remaining evidence closure.
Tracked group-style and one-undo-step implementations match the requirement; the outstanding work is precise ledger evidence linkage.
TextTab accepts free text and the renderer scans system fonts; no bundled-safe, preview-capable catalog owner exists.
The exact invariants and focused tests exist; the record requires evidence rebinding rather than a new product implementation.
Nine headings converge on one Inspector UI slice. Pure helper tests do not exercise component states, tabs, fields, scrubbing, and lanes.
These eleven heading-derived records belong to media search, not Inspector/text/keyframes, and duplicate one implemented search capability.
Tracked dispatch code routes InspectMedia, generation, upscale, and motion-graphic tools to an explicit not-yet-implemented result, directly contradicting production-reachability requirements.
Generation SDK building blocks exist, but Dispatcher does not call them and no complete placeholder, persistence, import, and N-result finalization path exists.

The advertised tool catalog does not provide complete production surfaces for tracking, matting, removal, color match, stem separation, translation, scripted assembly, avatars, and consent-gated voice cloning.
The tracked Chromium owner is an unavailable skeleton and the MCP Add/EditMotionGraphic route is an explicit stub, contradicting a production runner requirement.
Twenty-three heading-derived records converge on implemented, imported, and tested shared owners. They need exact evidence rebinding rather than per-heading product work.
Loading and registry owners exist, but no complete authoring, packaging, signing, and packaged-workflow validation lifecycle was found.
These are umbrella acceptance records for atomic writes, read-only proposals, linked synchronization, and the full agent call chain, not independent document-edit tasks.
Dispatcher explicitly returns a needs-vision-backend error; existing autocrop and planning building blocks are not wired to the production dispatch path.
Normalization and stable accounts are implemented and tested, while the broader negative secret-leakage contract lacks complete acceptance coverage.
The exact migration and precedence rules have focused owned tests; ledger evidence closure remains.
Loopback HTTP and basic guards exist, but stdio, exact resources, content-type and protocol guards, enabled preference, and metadata acceptance are incomplete.
The crate exports and Tauri imports are present; a narrow structural compile/export gate is needed before evidence closure.
Five heading records duplicate one implemented and tested short-ID contract; they require consolidated evidence closure.
Provider selection, SSE parsing, and tool-loop owners exist, but no explicit orphan tool-use repair owner or test was found.
No structured, correlation-stable, privacy-aware optional telemetry owner was found; scattered tracing is insufficient.
The generation call chain and Rust caption coverage exist; a focused MediaPanel UI generation, editing, and export acceptance remains.
No tracked feedback-submission owner was found.
No Sentry or DSN initialization owner was found; a settings label is not implementation evidence.

slices.rationale: Sixteen heading records converge on one shared token capability. Central owners and consumers exist, but there is no complete upstream-table and all-panel-consumption gate.
This is a release-level umbrella spanning sample projects, accessibility, visual polish, and interaction parity; no local test can close it alone.
Layout and focus owners exist, but current tests cover PanelShell focus only and not all presets, ratios, gutters, and surfaces.
The hook is mounted by App and covers Space and save, but the complete documented shortcut table is not implemented or tested as a matrix.
Cursor and hover behavior is scattered across multiple owners; one overlay test does not prove the complete table.
These six heading records belong to media transcription, not accessibility polish, and duplicate one implemented transcription capability.
All four records are unchecked audit-plan instructions saying to run a focused test and confirm failure; they are not product requirements and should be filtered by requirement extraction.
